paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The figure illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Sparse Deep Probabilistic Attention) output values in relation to different layers of a neural network, with a specific focus on the threshold of \(1 \times 10^{-2}\). The purpose of this plot is to depict the changes in sparsity across the layers.

The X-axis is labeled as "Layer," representing the layer numbers of the neural network. It employs a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 22, with equal intervals for each layer number. 

The Y-axis is designated as "Sparsity Ratio," which indicates the proportion of output values falling below the specified threshold. The scale here is also linear, starting from 0 to approximately 1.0, with equidistant numeric intervals typically at increments of 0.1.

The plot features three distinct lines representing different conditions of sparsity after gating:
1. The blue dashed line corresponds to the sparsity ratio before gating, which averages around \(0.03\). It starts near 1.0 at layer 0 and gradually decreases, approaching 0.0 by layer 22.
2. The orange dotted line represents the sparsity ratio after gating, exhibiting an average of \(0.44\). This line starts from a higher value near 1.0 but shows fluctuations as it progresses towards the latter layers.
3. The green dashed line indicates the sparsity ratio after the average gate, with an average of \(0.33\). This line generally trends downward, reflecting a gradual decrease in sparsity across the layers.

Overall, the graph captures the changes in sparsity ratios across the neural network layers, highlighting the differences between the sparsity measurements before gating, after gating, and after averaging the gate outputs.
model_annotations.Chinese:
The graph illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values as a function of layer number, specifically comparing the ratios before and after applying gating at a given threshold of 1e-2. On the x-axis, labeled as "Layer," the scale is linear with values ranging from 0 to 22, represented at uniform intervals. The y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also follows a linear scale from 0 to 1.

In the graph, three distinct lines are represented: a blue dashed line indicating the sparsity ratio before gating, which averages to 0.03. This line begins at approximately 1.0 at layer 0 and gradually decreases to around 0.0 by layer 22. The orange dotted line represents the sparsity ratio after gating, with an average of 0.44. This line shows a similar trend, starting higher and fluctuating around 0.3 to 0.4 after the initial drop. Finally, a green dashed line depicts the sparsity ratio after the average gate, averaging 0.33. This line trends downward, fluctuating slightly in value before stabilizing near 0.1 towards the end.
model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratios of SDPA output across different layers, with a threshold set at \(1 \times 10^{-2}\). The x-axis is labeled "Layer," with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 22, representing 23 total layers, with tick marks at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1, indicating the proportion of output values below the specified threshold. Three lines are depicted in the plot: one dashed blue line for the "sparsity ratio before gate," which starts at approximately 1.0 at layer 0 before declining gradually to around 0.1 at layer 22; a dotted orange line for the "sparsity ratio after gate," which begins at about 0.6, slightly fluctuates, and ends at approximately 0.4 at layer 22; and a dashed green line for the "sparsity ratio after average gate," which starts near 0.2 and trends downwards before leveling off closer to 0.1 at layer 22. Each line illustrates distinct trends in sparsity ratios throughout the layers, clearly showcasing their behavior in relation to the gating mechanisms applied.
model_annotations.German:
Das Diagramm zeigt das Verhältnis der Sparsamkeit des SDPA-Ausgangs in Abhängigkeit von der Schichtnummer, wobei ein Schwellenwert von 1e-2 verwendet wird. Die x-Achse ist als „Layer“ (Schicht) bezeichnet und reicht von 0 bis 22 mit einem gleichmäßigen, linearen Skalierungsschritt. Die y-Achse zeigt das Sparsamkeitsverhältnis mit einer Skala von 0 bis 1, ebenfalls in linearer Skala.

Es sind drei Linien im Diagramm dargestellt. Die blaue Linie, die durchgezogene Linie, repräsentiert das Sparsamkeitsverhältnis vor dem Gate mit einem durchschnittlichen Wert von 0,03. Diese Linie beginnt bei etwa 1,0 und fällt bis auf etwa 0,02 bei Layer 22. Die orangefarbene gepunktete Linie zeigt das Sparsamkeitsverhältnis nach dem Gate mit einem durchschnittlichen Wert von 0,44. Diese Linie beginnt bei etwa 0,95 und verläuft fallend, wobei sie in den Schichten 5 bis 10 einen plötzlichen Rückgang zeigt, bevor sie sich bei etwa 0,15 stabilisiert. Die grüne gestrichelte Linie stellt das Sparsamkeitsverhältnis nach dem durchschnittlichen Gate mit einem durchschnittlichen Wert von 0,33 dar. Diese Linie zeigt ebenfalls einen kontinuierlichen Rückgang, erreicht jedoch einen stabileren Verlauf ab Layer 10 mit einem Wert von ca. 0,05, bevor sie am Ende der x-Achse leicht ansteigt.
